subject_group: 10.1.5 Aerial refueling sensing, data, visual cues, and lighting systems compatibility

versions.text: Criterion: Verify that any viewing system which is to be used by any crewmember/ operator/automated system during the aerial refueling process is designed to permit safe aerial refueling operations. Standard: When viewing systems are to be used by any crewmember/operator/automated system in the tanker and/or receiver air vehicle during the aerial refueling process, each viewing system is designed such that it permits safe aerial refueling operations to be conducted. Design parameters to be considered include, but are not limited to: field of view, latency, depth perception, clarity, background effects, thermal signatures of tanker/receiver, blooming and glare effects, failure response, solar effects, and overlay considerations. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, inspection and review of documentation. Analysis of technical data and evaluation of the system by crewmember(s)/operator(s)/automated system(s) during ground simulation, ground test, and flight test verify that each viewing system supports the conduct of safe aerial refueling operations. References: MIL-HDBK-516: 9

Standard: Sensing system(s) (e.g., window, sensor, camera and display, sensor and detection algorithm) used during the AR process provides data, to flight crew or automated system, needed to conduct AR operations under mission-defined environmental conditions. Data needed to conduct AR includes but is not limited to targeted air vehicle relative position and rates of motion, refueling system location, and refueling system status. Mission-defined environmental conditions include day, night, dusk, twilight, with and without NVIS, ambient moonlight levels, diverse backgrounds (e.g., snow, ocean, desert, populated city lights, foliage dominant), above clouds, below clouds, and in clouds. Parameters that impact the performance of the sensing system include but are not limited to FOV, resolution, latency, integrity, availability, thermal signatures of air vehicles involved, bloom and glare effects, solar effects, operation with single failures, and overlaid information. a. Boom Tanker. Tanker air vehicle sensing system(s) provides situational awareness data required to accomplish AR with receptacle-equipped receivers. 1. Human Viewed System. Sensing system enables viewing of visual cues including boom nozzle, boom flight controls, boom structure, boom stability, boom movement (throughout boom envelope and during deployment and stowage), receiver receptacle, receiver stability, receiver movement, contours on top of receiver, receiver canopy, area around the receptacle, edges of slipway, edges of the receptacle, boom position relative to receiver, closure rate of receiver to contact position, antennas, wing leading edges, engine nacelles, horizontal/vertical stabilizers, receptacle bore, engagement of the boom in the slipway and receptacle, and receptacle doors. If sensing system is not direct view through a window, data acquisition system does not introduce misleading cues through depth distortions, insufficient contrast or extraneous visual artifacts. 2. Unmanned System. Sensing system provides needed data including air vehicle relative and absolute locations and sensor generated pose estimation of receiver receptacle. Data is received and interpreted within required parameters (e.g., integrity, availability, accuracy) to accomplish AR. b. Drogue Tanker. Tanker air vehicle sensing system(s) provides situational awareness data and visual cues needed to accomplish AR with probe-equipped receivers. 1. Human Viewed System. Sensing system enables viewing of visual cues including hose exit tunnel, drogue (from deployment, through extension to full trail), hose stability, receiver probe, receiver stability, receiver engagement profile, receiver movement in contact, and hose response in contact. 2. Unmanned System. Sensing system provides needed data including air vehicle relative and absolute locations. Data is received and interpreted within required parameters (e.g., integrity, availability, accuracy) to accomplish AR. c. Receptacle Receiver. Air vehicle sensing system(s) provides situational awareness data and visual cues needed to accomplish AR with boom-equipped tankers. 1. Human Viewed System. Sensing system enables viewing of visual cues including PDLs, refueling boom, formation lights, and formation markings. 2. Unmanned System. Sensing system provides needed data including air vehicle relative and absolute locations and sensor generated tanker relative position data. Data is received and interpreted within required parameters (e.g., integrity, availability, accuracy) to accomplish AR. d. Probe Receiver. Air vehicle sensing system provides situational awareness data and visual cues needed to accomplish AR with drogue-equipped tankers. 1. Human Viewed System. Sensing system enables viewing of visual cues including signal lights, hose markings, drogue, coupling, exit tunnel, air vehicle reference features, tanker underbody markings, and formation lights. 2. Unmanned System. Sensing system provides needed data including air vehicle relative and absolute locations and sensor generated pose estimation of tanker drogue. Data is received and interpreted within needed parameters (e.g., integrity, availability, accuracy) to accomplish AR. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of system specifications and system design verifies sensing system provides data to enable AR operations in all air vehicle environmental and mission conditions. Analysis.
  (1) Task analysis determines visual cues for human operated systems needed to accomplish AR with targeted air vehicles. Analysis of sensing system design and installation verifies data is provided in all air vehicle environmental and mission conditions.
  (2) Computer modeling of refueling tasks determines data and performance parameters needed to accomplish AR with targeted air vehicles. Analysis of sensing system design and installation verifies data is provided in all air vehicle environmental and mission conditions. Demonstration.
    (1) Air vehicle ground demonstration verifies sensing system provides and, if human viewed, accurately displays data and visual cues needed to conduct AR in simulated environmental and mission environments. Test.
      (1) Lab test: Hardware-in-the-loop laboratory testing verifies sensing system provides, and if human viewed, accurately displays, data and visual cues required to conduct AR in simulated environmental and mission environments.
      (2) Ground test: Air vehicle ground testing verifies sensing system provides and, if human viewed, accurately displays data and visual cues needed to conduct AR in simulated environmental and mission environments. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
      (3) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. 1. Human Operator. Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies situation awareness data and visual cues needed to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions are provided and, if not directly viewed, accurately displayed. Test points include various ambient lighting conditions (e.g., day, night, dusk), receiver join up, astern, contact position, receiver positions throughout the boom envelope, multiple receivers and if utilizing visual sensors (remote vision systems), high and low sun angles, various direction headings, and background conditions. 2. Unmanned System. Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies sensing system receives data within parameters needed to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions. Test points include receiver join up, astern, contact position, contact, and disconnect. Stressing test conditions depend on the method of data acquisition (e.g., differential GPS, lidar, visible cameras). b. Drogue Tanker. 1. Human Operator. Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies situation awareness data/visual cues needed to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions are provided and, if not directly viewed, accurately displayed. Test points include various ambient lighting conditions (e.g., day, night, dusk), receiver join up, pre-contact, contact, in-contact maneuvering, different receivers, and if utilizing visual sensors (remote vision systems), high and low sun angles, various direction headings, and background conditions. 2. Unmanned System. Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies sensing system receives data within parameters needed to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions. Test points include receiver join-up, pre-contact, contact, and in-contact maneuvering. Stressing test conditions depend on the method of data acquisition (e.g., differential GPS, lidar, visible cameras). c. Receptacle Receiver. 1. Human Operator. Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies situation awareness data and visual cues required to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions are provided and, if not directly viewed, accurately displayed. Test points include various ambient lighting conditions (e.g., day, night, dusk), with and without NVIS, join up, astern, contact position, throughout the boom envelope, and if utilizing visual sensors (remote vision systems), high and low sun angles, various direction headings, and background conditions. 2. Unmanned System. Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies sensing system receives data within parameters needed to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions. Test points include join up, astern, contact position, and throughout the boom envelope. Stressing conditions depend on the method of data acquisition (e.g., differential GPS, lidar, visible cameras). d. Probe Receiver. 1. Human Operator. Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies situation awareness data and visual cues needed to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions are provided and, if not directly viewed, accurately displayed. Test points include various ambient lighting conditions (e.g. day, night, dusk), with and without NVIS, join up, pre-contact, contact, in contact maneuvering, and if utilizing visual sensors (remote vision systems), high and low sun angles, various direction headings and background conditions. 2. Unmanned System. Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies sensing system receives data within parameters needed to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions are provided and, if not directly viewed, accurately displayed. Test points include join up, pre-contact, contact, and in-contact maneuvering. Stressing conditions depend on the method of data acquisition (e.g., differential GPS, lidar, visible cameras).
